newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Eximbank says capital increase needed.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Eximbank says capital increase needed.

text.p: Hungary's state-owned Eximbank needs a fivefold capital increase to fulfil its role in promoting Hungarian exports, General Manager Ivan Nyiri said on Monday.
"This bank should be working with a capital of 20 billion to 25 billion forints, not (the current) five billion," Nyiri told a news conference following the bank's annual general meeting.
He added there were no plans for a capital increase this year but that the bank hoped it would eventually happen.
Eximbank's capital adequacy ratio shrunk to 66 percent at the end of 1996 from 355 percent a year before, Nyiri said.
He added that Eximbank and state-owned export loan insurer MEHIB Rt, of which he is also general manager, between them last year facilitated 3.2 percent of Hungary's exports.
Nyiri said the two companies' long-term goal was to raise this ratio to some seven percent.
"It would be unreasonable to aim for anything higher than that," he said.
The bank plans to double its balance sheet total from 12 billion forints at the end of 1996, Nyiri said, adding that at the moment its balance sheet stood at some 18 billion forints.
He added that the bank's activity was also hindered by a delay in passing a new bill -- prepared with the bank's cooperation -- to ease conditions on export financing.
"It is very important for the bill to be passed very soon and without any changes," Nyiri said.
